source_regions.interpretation: conditional Gibbs potential and phase law (3.1)

legitimate_route_at_most_seven_steps: Use genuine C2 lower Hessian bound to obtain StrongConvexOn univ alpha V, then existing positive-modulus Gibbs integrability. No critical point or minimizing point is needed.
For fixed y, eta>0 gives Vy(y,x)>=V(x), hence 0<exp(-Vy)<=exp(-V). Continuity supplies measurability; Integrable.mono' gives integrability. integral_exp_pos over nonzero canonical volume yields Zx>0.
Use existing Gaussian integral at coefficient 1/2: integral exp(-norm(p)^2/2)=C=(sqrt(2*pi))^finrank>0. Equivalently specialize the existing isotropic Gaussian density theorem at variance 1.
Split exp(-U)=exp(-Vy)*exp(-norm(p)^2/2). Tonelli on position-first volume.prod volume gives Zphase=ofReal(Zx*C), using nonnegativity and the real/ENNReal integral bridge.
Zx>0 and C>0 give Zphase>0; ofReal of a real number is finite. The existing normalized Gibbs withDensity theorem then gives IsProbabilityMeasure nu.

Expand Measure.tilted at -Vy, giving density ofReal(exp(-Vy)/Zx); specialize stdGaussian density at variance 1 giving ofReal(C^(-1)*exp(-norm(p)^2/2)). Derive both as measurable exact representatives.

Use prod_withDensity and positivity-compatible ofReal multiplication/division/inverse identities to identify the product density with Zphase^(-1)*ofReal(exp(-U)). No process, event-simplex, sector substitution or invariance lemma is needed.
independent_dependency_edges: Hessian lower bound + C2 -> strong convexity of V -> exp(-V) integrable
eta positive + exp(-V) integrable -> exp(-Vy) integrable -> Zx positive
Gaussian integral + product factorization + position integrability -> exact finite positive phase mass
finite positive phase mass -> probability nu
tilted representative + Gaussian density + exact phase mass + product-density theorem -> product-law identification
optional_alternative: QuadraticRegularization can instead derive strong convexity of Vy. It is not required by the smaller domination route.
not_a_dependency: SAU102 weighted-sector substitution is analytically independent of normalization; both meet only at a future normalized averaging consumer.
zero_dimension: Canonical volume on the zero vector space has mass 1, C=1, Zx=exp(-V(0))>0, phase normalization cancels that scalar, and both marginals are the unit atom.
six_hypotheses: hAlpha>0, hAlphaBeta, hV C2, two-sided genuine Hessian hH, hEta>0, hBetaEta. Upper bound/order/upper scale are retained source binders but not needed for this smaller normalization argument.
no_hidden_provider: No supplied minimizer, gradient zero, lower envelope, finite normalizer, probability assumption or density provider.
scope: Prospective header and dependency feasibility only; no proof, claim, seal, VERIFIED or process invariance.
